title: Maximum Value of a String
approach_name: Compare numeric values and nonnumeric string lengths
notes:
Task and constraints: Treat digit-only strings as integers and other strings by length.
Idea: Compare numeric values and nonnumeric string lengths.
Technique and why it applies: a bounded traversal applies the condition to each relevant item, which directly matches the operation required. Method/code entry point: maximumValue().
Invariant: The best score is the largest numeric value or string length seen among processed entries.
Edge cases: Digit-only strings are parsed numerically; other strings use length.
Complexity: Time O(nm); auxiliary space O(1).
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int maximumValue(String[] strs){int best=0;for(String s:strs){boolean numeric=true;for(char c:s.toCharArray())if(!Character.isDigit(c)){numeric=false;break;}best=Math.max(best,numeric?Integer.parseInt(s):s.length());}return best;} }
complexity_reason: The compare numeric values and nonnumeric string lengths implementation follows its stated loops and data structures.

title: Delete Greatest Value in Each Row

notes:

Idea: Sort each row and sum column maxima.

code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int deleteGreatestValue(int[][] grid){for(int[] r:grid)Arrays.sort(r);int ans=0;for(int j=0;j<grid[0].length;j++){int m=0;for(int[] r:grid)m=Math.max(m,r[j]);ans+=m;}return ans;} }

title: Count Pairs Of Similar Strings
approach_name: Count pairs with identical sets of letters
notes:
Task and constraints: Count pairs whose words have the same set of letters.
Idea: Count pairs with identical sets of letters.
Technique and why it applies: a set supports membership or distinct-value checks; two pointers process opposing ends, which directly matches the operation required. Method/code entry point: similarPairs().
Invariant: The pair count includes exactly pairs whose character sets are equal, independent of letter order.
Edge cases: Repeated letters do not change a word's distinct-character set.
Complexity: Time O(n^2*m); auxiliary space O(n*m).
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int similarPairs(String[] words){int n=words.length,c=0;Set<Character>[] sets=new Set[n];for(int i=0;i<n;i++){sets[i]=new HashSet<>();for(char x:words[i].toCharArray())sets[i].add(x);}for(int i=0;i<n;i++)for(int j=i+1;j<n;j++)if(sets[i].equals(sets[j]))c++;return c;} }
complexity_reason: The count pairs with identical sets of letters implementation follows its stated loops and data structures.

title: Maximum Enemy Forts That Can Be Captured

Idea: Count zeros between opposite nonzero forts.

Edge cases: Same-sign forts do not bound a capturable segment.
Complexity: Time O(n); auxiliary space O(1).
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int captureForts(int[] forts){int best=0,prev=-1;for(int i=0;i<forts.length;i++)if(forts[i]!=0){if(prev>=0&&forts[i]==-forts[prev])best=Math.max(best,i-prev-1);prev=i;}return best;} }

title: Minimum Common Value

notes:

Technique and why it applies: two pointers process opposing ends, which directly matches the operation required. Method/code entry point: getCommon().
Invariant: The pointers discard only values too small to match the current value in the other sorted array.
Edge cases: If a pointer exhausts its array without a match, return -1.
Complexity: Time O(n+m); auxiliary space O(1).
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int getCommon(int[] nums1,int[] nums2){int i=0,j=0;while(i<nums1.length&&j<nums2.length){if(nums1[i]==nums2[j])return nums1[i];if(nums1[i]<nums2[j])i++;else j++;}return -1;} }
